card.name: Spots where 'many' would come next
card.fires_on: Words in general web text right before a plural noun or verb that a quantity word like 'many' could naturally lead into, such as 'keeps popping up', 'we hear about', 'rising number of', 'more reports'. It fires on the word just before that slot.

modes.label: Recurring or growing trends
modes.description: Verbs or nouns describing something that keeps happening or is increasing, before the thing being counted.
modes.example: keeps popping<< up>>. This time, researchers say that children

modes.label: Quantity phrases
modes.description: Words like 'number of', 'more', 'few' or 'most' that lead into a counted plural noun.
modes.example: The rising number<< of>> cases has forced some companies,

modes.label: Hearing about cases
modes.description: Verbs of reporting such as 'hear' or 'about' before plural examples.
modes.example: Continually we<< hear>> about students cheating on tests.

card.writes: It lowers the chance of 'many' words in English and Chinese, so the output moves away from vague quantity words.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to talk about plural things, and it makes the model less likely to say 'many'.
